title: Hard hearts in a boat (Mark 8:11–21)
hook: they've forgotten bread and worry, after two feedings

segments.voice: Yesterday, seven baskets: four thousand fed in Gentile country. Your line was enough again.

One loaf. That's the whole inventory. A few verses back, seven baskets of leftovers. Now the disciples are crossing the lake again, somebody checks the bag, and Mark says they had forgotten to take bread: one loaf with them, and that's all. It's the wallet-left-on-the-counter moment, out on the water. While they mutter about lunch, Jesus is trying to tell them something else entirely. They miss it, and Mark doesn't tidy the scene up for them.
screen: `ONE LOAF IN THE BOAT.` → `THE BREAD THEY FORGOT.` → `THEY MISS WHAT HE SAYS.`

segments.voice: Just before they sailed, some Pharisees had asked Jesus for a sign from heaven, proof on demand. He sighed deeply and refused: no sign will be given to this generation. Now in the boat he warns, in the old King James Bible: "Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod." Leaven, you might remember from day twenty-four, is the bit of old dough that works invisibly through a whole batch. Mark doesn't define it here. Some readers take it as an attitude that spreads: demanding proof, playing power games. And the disciples say to each other, he's talking about bread because we forgot to bring any. So the questions come fast: "perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened? Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?" Then a quiz. When I broke five loaves for five thousand, how many baskets of leftovers? Twelve, they say. And the seven for four thousand? Seven. And he says, "How is it that ye do not understand?" No answer. They've watched thousands fed, twice, and they're worried about lunch with him sitting right there. And notice the one loaf in the boat. Some readers hear a quiet hint: they're not as short of bread as they think, because the one who fed the crowds is on board. Mark leaves them there, mid-crossing, with two counts of baskets and one loaf in the bag.
screen: `NO SIGN FOR THIS GENERATION.` · `BEWARE THE LEAVEN.` · `TWELVE BASKETS, THEN SEVEN.` · `ONE LOAF, AND HE'S ON BOARD.`

segments.voice: Go back to a time you were sure you wouldn't make it, when money, time, strength or hope was short, and somehow there was enough: someone showed up, a door opened, you got through. Count the baskets, so to speak: what was left over afterward? Hold that memory next to whatever you're worried about today, and if you pray, you can give thanks for that time.
Leaven, the old dough that works invisibly through a whole batch, Jesus's warning about an attitude that spreads, right before a quiz about two feedings.
Your line: do you not yet understand? Mark leaves the question hanging in the boat. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians keep a habit of remembering God's help in the past, through gratitude journals, testimonies or prayers of thanksgiving, as a way of meeting present worries.
